title: Lease-based traffic allocator for tiered plans and token burst protection
creator: Amelia Chen
description: Introduce a lease-based traffic allocator that issues short-lived credit slots (leases) to tenant requests to enforce plan-level quotas while preserving latency SLAs. Leases smooth short token bursts, allow fast admission decisions at the edge, and carry metadata used for regional affinity and model-variant fallbacks. This ticket covers design, prototype, and integration with the admission controller and router.
acceptance_criteria: System can grant and revoke per-tenant leases in < 10ms during admission path
Burst smoothing reduces token spike failures for free-tier tenants by >= 70% under synthetic load
When quota is exhausted, router demotes traffic to paid-compatible model variants or triggers grace-window leases according to policy
Telemetry surfaces lease grant/revoke rates, expiry distribution, and top callers by token leakage
E2E tests for regional affinity + lease handoff succeed across two regions with simulated capacity loss
design_notes: Lease concept: small immutable token (UUID) with TTL, token budget, tier tag, region hint, and fallback-model-hint. Issued from a global allocator service replicated per-region.
Allocation policy: prefer local-region allocation if healthy; allow soft-acceptance from adjacent region when local saturates (configurable per plan)
Lease lifetime: default 8s, adjustable by tenant class. Short TTL enables rapid reclamation and fine-grained accounting.
Budget accounting: each lease carries a remaining_tokens counter; runtime decrements on accepted requests until 0, then lease considered drained.
Grace behavior: free-tier can receive a short grace-lease beyond quota when operator-configured (burst allowance) with lower model-quality variant and additive logging for billing analysis.

Fallbacks: router maps tier tag + fallback-model-hint to a ranked list of model variants (same architecture w/ lower cost quantization or smaller model). When lease absent, router attempts fallback variant admission with degraded SLA target.
Lease cache: edge nodes maintain a short LRU cache of active leases to avoid frequent allocator calls for multi-request flows.
Telemetry: expose metrics for lease_issued, lease_revoked, lease_missed, lease_drain_latency, per-tier_lease_burn_rate, regional_handoffs
implementation_steps: API: define /leases/create and /leases/refresh endpoints with minimal payload and opaque lease token
Allocator: implement in allocator service with strong eventual consistency across replicas; leverage conditional increment counters per-tenant
Router integration: admission path reads lease token; if absent, attempt local allocator call or fallback decision chain
Edge cache: implement LRU cache + background refresh to reduce allocator QPS for hot flows
Model mapping: add config table to Console for mapping tier -> fallback variants and quality-preserving sampler parameters
Tests: synthetic load tests for burst scenarios, chaos test simulating region outage and lease handoff, integration test with billing telemetry
Docs: update API docs and Console guide on configuring burst allowances and fallback policies
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal rollout to staging; enable for internal tenants only; verify metrics and SLA impact
Beta: opt-in for select free + paid customers with monitoring dashboards and feature flag
GA: enable by default for free tier with conservative defaults; open controls in Console for escalation
Fallback kill-switch: operator toggle to disable lease-based admission and fall back to legacy quota checks
monitoring_signals: fallback_invocation.count and resulting model_quality regression alerts
token_failure_rate (requests denied due to quota) pre/post rollout
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: allocator becomes single-point of latency. Mitigation: local caches, aggressive timeouts, pre-warming leases for known bursty flows
Risk: inaccurate budget accounting causing overcommit. Mitigation: conservative initial budgets, periodic reconciliation jobs, and compensating refunds/logs
Risk: fallback variants degrade customer experience. Mitigation: A/B test quality, tie fallbacks to non-critical routes, and surface quality-impact dashboards
Risk: cross-region lease handoff complexity. Mitigation: implement staged handoff with telemetry and fail-open policy when handoff fails
